page_metadata.title: Development and Evaluation of Amorphous Solid Dispersion of Riluzole with PBPK Model to Simulate the Pharmacokinetic Profile

model_classification.evidence_quote: The PBPK model can predict RLZ concentration in multiple compartments including plasma and liver.

model_context.model_origin: new rat PBPK model, then extrapolated to humans
model_context.stated_purpose: Predict riluzole concentration-time profiles and compare Rilutor versus RLZ:PAA amorphous solid dispersion exposure
model_context.dose_metric: plasma and brain Cmax/AUC; concentrations in multiple compartments

stated_assumptions.description: Human physiological parameters were changed relative to rat and biochemical parameters were scaled using the allometric relationship.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: For human, physiological parameters were changed along with a biochemical parameter.

stated_assumptions.description: Only three biopharmaceutical parameters were changed for the ASD formulation.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: For ASD formulation, the three biopharmaceutical parameters were changed: gut absorption rate, undissolved drug in feces, and bile rate constant.

absorption.evidence_quote: Oral dosing is represented through gastric emptying and a first-order gut absorption rate constant.

metabolism.evidence_quote: RLZ-OH is the major metabolite, mainly produced by CYP1A2 followed by UGT1A1; riluzole metabolism is modeled with Michaelis-Menten kinetics.

elimination.evidence_quote: Elimination occurs by urine from kidney and feces from gut.

unresolved.description: Figure 1 caption states a nine-compartment PBPK model, while the displayed list includes plasma plus stomach, gut, liver, brain, kidney, lung, fat, heart and rest body.
unresolved.reason: The source is internally inconsistent if plasma is counted as a modeled compartment; extraction preserves the stated count and the displayed labels.

allometric_scaling_rules: Human physiological parameters changed and selected biochemical parameters scaled/allometrically adjusted

verification.summary: Updated audited extraction: preserves the nine-versus-ten compartment discrepancy and additionally captures ASD-specific narrative parameters that are named in the paper but not numerically tabulated.

flags.message: Figure 1 is captioned as a nine-compartment PBPK model, while the displayed labels include 10 modeled compartments when plasma is counted.
Bile rate constant and undissolved drug in feces are stated as ASD-specific changes but are not numerically reported in Table I.
